title: Implement incremental snapshot checkpoint and compatibility gatekeeper
author: Asha Patel
body: Problem and motivation: Upgrades for private deployments currently rely on full-snapshot handoffs and operator-coordinated rollbacks. This approach has two shortcomings: (1) large snapshots increase upgrade time and blast radius when a migration needs to be reverted, and (2) upgrades lack an automatic check that guarantees schema + runtime compatibility for downgrades. This PR introduces an incremental snapshot checkpoint protocol plus a compatibility gatekeeper service that validates downgrade safety during preflight and runtime rollbacks. Summary of changes: - Introduces an incremental snapshot format and on-disk checkpoint manifest with atomic commit semantics. Checkpoints are written as a sequence of chunked deltas with a final commit marker; operators can perform partial restores to any checkpoint in the chain. - Adds a compatibility gatekeeper daemon that runs preflight checks and lightweight runtime validations to detect downgrade-incompatible schema changes or irreversible migration steps. The gatekeeper produces a human-readable report and machine-friendly exit codes for automation. - Adds Helm hooks and a Terraform module flag to enable staged checkpointing during upgrades: when enabled, the installer creates a checkpoint before each migration batch and records a checkpoint token in the release metadata. - Adds a restore-dryrun utility (rpictl restore --dry-run --checkpoint <token>) which executes a simulated restore against a temporary, ephemeral namespace and reports regressions. - Improves operator reconciliation so that rollbacks prefer checkpoint restoration over full cluster rollbacks when a matching checkpoint token exists. - Adds e2e tests (integration/restore_checkpoints_test.go) that run a multi-tenant migration, produce checkpoints, and validate partial restores and rollback gating. Rollout plan and risk mitigation: - Default behavior is opt-in via helm value privateInstaller.checkpointing.enable=false; chart default remains disabled to avoid impacting current users. - Add gradual rollout in Redwood-managed deployments: enable for 10% of upgrade jobs, collect restore success rate and gatekeeper false-positive rate, then expand. - If a gatekeeper report contains an explicit irreversible-change flag, the operator will block the automated rollback and escalate to manual review. Checklist: - [x] Design and protobufs for checkpoint manifest - [x] Persistence layer + atomic commit protocol - [x] Compatibility gatekeeper service + report format - [x] Helm hooks and chart values - [x] Terraform flag and documentation - [x] rpictl restore dry-run CLI - [x] Integration and e2e tests - [x] Docs and runbook updates How to test locally: 1) Build operator image: make build-operator 2) Deploy chart with checkpointing enabled: helm upgrade --install redwood-installer ./charts/redwood-private-installer -f ci/values/checkpoint-enabled.yaml 3) Run a migration scenario from ci/testdata and create checkpoints: make ci-run-migration 4) Dry-run a restore with: rpictl restore --dry-run --checkpoint <token> 5) Inspect gatekeeper report at /var/run/gatekeeper/report.json Rollback/merge notes: This is implemented as a feature-flagged change and can be rolled back by disabling privateInstaller.checkpointing.enable and redeploying the chart. In the unlikely event of restore incompatibility, operator logs include the checkpoint manifest and a sha256 for reproducible debugging. Related: ENG-2749 (migration reliability), ENG-2891 (restore automation).
commits: feat(checkpoint): add incremental checkpoint protobuf and persistence + atomic commit
feat(gatekeeper): initial compatibility gatekeeper daemon and report schema
chore(helm): add pre-upgrade and post-upgrade hooks for checkpoint lifecycle
feat(cli): add rpictl restore --dry-run and checkpoint listing
refactor(operator): prefer checkpoint restore path in rollback reconciler
test(e2e): add integration tests for checkpoint creation and partial restore
docs: add runbook and helm value documentation
review_comments: Liam Nguyen: Please add unit tests for the checkpoint commit/abort window; I saw a race in the first run. Can you also quantify the worst-case snapshot size overhead?
Asha Patel: Added commit/abort unit tests and a size estimator to checkpoint_store.go; documented overhead (~3-6% typical for delta encoding).
Sofia Martinez: Gatekeeper looks good; request to make the irreversible-change flag explicit in the report and to add an operator metric for gatekeeper block count.
Asha Patel: Made irreversible-change an explicit field and added metrics.redwood_gatekeeper_block_count (counter).
Ethan Brown: CI flaky on e2e restore dry-run on first run (timeout); increased retry/backoff in test harness. CI passed after rerun.
merge_commit_message:
Implement incremental snapshot checkpoint and compatibility gatekeeper

- incremental checkpoints with atomic commit
- compatibility gatekeeper + report
- helm hooks + terraform flag
- rpictl restore dry-run
- operator prefer checkpoint restore path

Refs: ENG-2749, ENG-2891
release_notes: Add opt-in incremental checkpointing and a compatibility gatekeeper for private deployments. This enables faster, lower-risk rollbacks via partial restores to checkpoints and provides automated downgrade safety checks. Feature is behind helm value privateInstaller.checkpointing.enable and is disabled by default. See docs/runbooks/checkpointing.md for upgrade instructions.
